references.text: Moses inspected the work and saw that they had done everything just as the Lord had commanded. This shows the same pattern of obedience to the Lord's commands.
Moses carried out the work 'just as the Lord had commanded him,' a recurring phrase throughout chapter 40 that confirms his faithful obedience.
Another example of Moses acting 'just as the Lord had commanded him' in setting up the tabernacle.
Moses continues to do everything according to the Lord's command, emphasizing the main theme of the verse.
The repetition of 'just as the Lord had commanded Moses' shows consistent obedience throughout the entire process.
Moses burns fragrant incense 'just as the Lord had commanded him,' confirming his faithfulness.
Moses sets up the altar for burnt offerings 'just as the Lord had commanded him.'
Describes how Moses and Aaron washed themselves 'just as the Lord had commanded Moses.'
Moses did as the Lord had commanded him, a similar expression of obedience to God's commands.
Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him, and the Israelites obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses was faithful in all God's house, referring to his faithful service in carrying out everything the Lord commanded.
The book of Hebrews quotes that Moses was warned to do everything according to the pattern shown to him on the mountain, linking it to his precise obedience.
Highlights how the obedience of the leader (Moses) and the people together completes God's plan for the tabernacle.
Complementary verses that together document the complete obedience in the building of the tabernacle.
A summarizing verse confirming that all the work on the tabernacle was completed in perfect obedience.
